questions.questionText: Of 145 customers at a Mumbai mall, 5 pay using neither a credit card nor PhonePe. 80 pay using a credit card and 78 pay using PhonePe. How many pay using both?

questions.shortcut: Both = A + B − (Total − Neither).

questions.questionText: Every one of the families in a Madurai colony watch at least one of Pro Kabaddi and ISL. 2/3 of them watch Pro Kabaddi, 5/6 of them watch ISL, and 9 watch both. How many people are there in the group?
questions.explanation: Everyone is in at least one set, so fa + fb − Both fraction = 1. Both fraction = 2/3 + 5/6 − 1 = 1/2. Total = 9 ÷ 1/2 = 18.
questions.shortcut: Both fraction = fa + fb − 1 (when nobody is outside); Total = Both ÷ that fraction.

questions.questionText: Every one of the farmers in a Punjab village grow at least one of rice and sugarcane. 3/4 of them grow rice, 2/3 of them grow sugarcane, and 30 grow both. How many people are there in the group?

questions.questionText: Every one of the students in a Chennai college play at least one of kabaddi and football. 5/8 of them play kabaddi, 1/2 of them play football, and 5 play both. How many people are there in the group?

questions.shortcut: Both fraction = fa + fb − 1 (when nobody is outside); Total = Both ÷ that fraction.

questions.questionText: Of 87 people at a Kolkata book fair, 20 read neither The Hindu nor Anandabazar Patrika, and 22 read both. The number who read only The Hindu and the number who read only Anandabazar Patrika are in the ratio 3 : 2. How many read The Hindu (in all)?
questions.explanation: Only The Hindu + only Anandabazar Patrika = 87 − 20 − 22 = 45. Split 3:2 → 3k + 2k = 45, k = 9, only The Hindu = 27. Total The Hindu = 27 + 22 = 49.
questions.shortcut: Remove Neither and Both first; split the rest in the given ratio; add Both back.

questions.questionText: Of 80 farmers in a Punjab village, 20 grow neither maize nor rice, and 24 grow both. The number who grow only maize and the number who grow only rice are in the ratio 2 : 1. How many grow maize (in all)?
questions.explanation: Only maize + only rice = 80 − 20 − 24 = 36. Split 2:1 → 2k + 1k = 36, k = 12, only maize = 24. Total maize = 24 + 24 = 48.
questions.shortcut: Remove Neither and Both first; split the rest in the given ratio; add Both back.

questions.questionText: Of 78 farmers in a Punjab village, 15 grow neither wheat nor sugarcane, and 7 grow both. The number who grow only wheat and the number who grow only sugarcane are in the ratio 4 : 3. How many grow wheat (in all)?
questions.explanation: Only wheat + only sugarcane = 78 − 15 − 7 = 56. Split 4:3 → 4k + 3k = 56, k = 8, only wheat = 32. Total wheat = 32 + 7 = 39.
questions.shortcut: Remove Neither and Both first; split the rest in the given ratio; add Both back.

questions.questionText: Of 135 students in a Chennai college, 15 play neither football nor kabaddi, and 29 play both. The number who play only football and the number who play only kabaddi are in the ratio 4 : 3. How many play football (in all)?
questions.explanation: Only football + only kabaddi = 135 − 15 − 29 = 91. Split 4:3 → 4k + 3k = 91, k = 13, only football = 52. Total football = 52 + 29 = 81.
questions.shortcut: Remove Neither and Both first; split the rest in the given ratio; add Both back.
